QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_40

question.text: Ms. Sonia Rao, Fund Controller at Vindhya Capital (Cat I), is preparing the 180-day annual LP report. Which of the following is NOT among the material risks Category I and II AIFs must disclose in their annual report?

answer.text: Foreign exchange risk at fund level.
Daily NAV striking mechanism and series-of-units accounting methodology at fund level.
Extra-financial (ESG) risks at fund and investee-company level.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 22 and Chapter 12 list the risk disclosures: (i) concentration risk (fund level), (ii) FX risk (fund level), (iii) leverage risk (fund and investee), (iv) realisation risk (exit env) at fund and investee, (v) strategy risk (investee), (vi) reputation risk (investee), (vii) ESG risks (fund and investee). Daily NAV / series-of-units is a Cat III accounting mechanic, NOT a Cat I/II disclosure item. The Trap: The daily-NAV option is a deliberate Cat III cross-contamination trap — test-writers frequently embed Cat III accounting in Cat I/II contexts. Reject on sight for XIX-D. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers all 7 risk types. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) covers daily NAV and series-of-units. XIX-E (Cat III Manager) will drill the NAV mechanic — XIX-D does NOT. Manager's Pro-Tip: In the annual LP report, devote a dedicated 1-page matrix (risk type x fund vs investee level x mitigation) — sophisticated LPs scan this first. Bland boilerplate here is a Fund II kill-shot.
